newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral asks Kashmiris to focus on economy.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral asks Kashmiris to focus on economy.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral, on his first visit to the troubled Kashmir region after assuming office, on Sunday urged its people to shed sectarian feelings and concentrate on economic development.

The United News of India (UNI) quoted Gujral as saying that India needed to boost growth and at the same time step up poverty alleviation programmes to achieve the objective of social justice for all.
India achieved economic growth of 7.1 percent in 1995/96 (April-March). Gujral's centre-left coalition is seeking sustainable growth of 8.0 percent over a medium term.

Gujral was speaking at Jammu, winter capital of Jammu and Kashmir state, mainly Hindu India's only Moslem-majority province, where separatists are campaigning. Jammu is in the predominantly-Hindu southern part of the Himalayan state.
Gujral's choice of the state for his first visit out of the capital as prime minister was seen as a signal that Kashmir is on his list of priorities.

Since 1990, when simmering discontent erupted into a major rebellion, more than 20,000 people have been killed in the region disputed by Pakistan. India and Pakistan have fought two wars over Kashmir since independence from Britain in 1947.
India controls two thirds of the region and accuses Pakistan of supporting an armed rebellion in the state. Pakistan, which controls the remaining third, denies the charges.

Gujral was sworn in as the country's 12th prime minister last Monday after his United Front changed its previous leader, H.D. Deve Gowda, in order to win back vital parliamentary support from the Congress party.
